h: A Victorian Showstopper, Head to Toe
p: When the Tower opened in 1894, it was Blackpool's answer to the Eiffel Tower in Paris, and it's been the town's signature ever since. It rises to around 158 metres, and the views from the top stretch along the Fylde coast. On really clear days people often say they can pick out the Lake District hills and even the Isle of Man, so keep your eyes peeled if the skies play ball.

The SkyWalk glass floor is the part everyone talks about. Some people stride straight out; others need a good five minutes of encouragement, and that's half the fun. If you've got a nervous one in the group, let them watch everybody else survive first.

Timing makes a big difference. A sunny morning gives you crisp views out to sea, while late afternoon can bring a beautiful golden light over the Promenade. During Illuminations season, a visit as it gets dark can show off the lights stretching along the front, though check that the top is open that late before you plan around it.

Combine it with other parts of the Tower if you can: the Ballroom is a real wow moment, and the Circus is a family favourite. Bundle tickets can make sense if you're doing a few. After that, grab chips, find a bench on the front and look back up at where you've just been.
